doi_convention: A null publication_doi indicates that a DOI was not identified in the consulted materials.

CZ39.selection: 39 contemporary station columns (rec) from Table S1, checked against station codes in corrected Table S2. Historical columns are excluded.

IT28.citation: M. Adorni and L. Ghillani (2020). Indagine floristica nelle stazioni ferroviarie della provincia di Parma (Emilia-Romagna, Italia). Annali del Museo Civico di Rovereto 36, 149–200.
IT28.selection: Reconstruct station lists from enumerated station codes in the published flora.

MIREN.citation: MIREN survey of plant species in mountains, dataset v3
MIREN.role: Foreign roadside donors in Czechia and Italy, supplementary receiving-country road reference in India
MIREN.selection: Select roadside Plot 1 under protocols v.2017 or v.2022 and retain the first qualifying survey year per region, road and site. Give sites equal weight within a road and roads equal weight within each country.

SI89.citation: Šabić et al. (2026), study of Slovenian railway vegetation and microhabitats
SI89.selection: Use the union of ballast shoulder and toe records at the 89 retained sites. Map observed EPPO codes through the publisher’s taxon codebook.

HR_BA15.citation: N. Jasprica, M. Milović, K. Dolina and A. Lasić (2017). Analyses of the flora of railway stations in the Mediterranean and sub-Mediterranean areas of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Natura Croatica 26, 271–303.
HR_BA15.selection: Retain all 15 stations in the original species-by-station table as one study.

SK30.citation: Climate and traffic volume control plant species richness in railway areas (2025), Flora 330, 152780.
SK30.selection: Use printed occupancy percentages in Table S1. Each printed value maps uniquely to an occupied-station count out of 30. Mask ambiguous taxon-key marginals. Station-level species combinations are unavailable.

Kashmir.citation: Rashid et al. (2021), Journal of Applied Ecology, and accompanying Dryad data, version 99735.
Kashmir.role: Recipient railway survey and local interior reference
Kashmir.selection: Use 2014 station transects with all four quadrats observed. For each station, combine Track and Embankment for the railway frequency and Interior Plot 1 and Interior Plot 2 for the paired reference.

TreePits.citation: Tree-circles spontaneous vegetation over a long climatic gradient (2020), Urban Ecosystems.
TreePits.role: Urban references for Slovenia and the Adriatic recipient
TreePits.selection: Use published marginal frequencies in the four selected city columns. For the Adriatic recipient, average the two Croatian cities and weight the Croatian and Bosnian frequencies 13:2 to match the railway survey’s station allocation.

Malacky.citation: A. Rendeková (2016). Overview of ruderal plant communities of Malacky city. Acta Botanica Universitatis Comenianae 51, Table 1.
Malacky.selection: Parse the 18 relevés in Table 1, including the separately listed singleton records, and exclude relevé 15, identified as a railway plot.

WA.citation: ENV Australia Pty Ltd (2008). Rapid Growth Project 5: Jimblebar Junction to Yandi Junction Railway Reserve Flora and Vegetation Assessment. Final report 08.165 RP001.
WA.role: Geographic extension using Western Australian railway-reserve vegetation
WA.selection: Intersect the individually documented 2,500 m² plots with Appendix I matrix site identifiers and Appendix G sheets containing in-plot observations. Use taxon records from Appendix G, excluding records flagged outside the plot (OP).
WA.cohort_hash_encoding: UTF-8 of sorted original plot IDs, newline separated, including a final newline.
